content:
Part 1: DNA Repair and End-Prep

    Step 1.1: Dilute the DNA Control Sample (DCS).

        Option 1.1.1: Prepare diluted DNA Control Sample.
            - DNA Control Sample: 35 µL
            - Elution Buffer: 105 µL

    Step 1.2: Prepare DNA samples for the repair and end-prep reaction.

        Option 1.2.1: Prepare sample mix by combining the following components.
            - purified DNA samples: 11 µL
            - nuclease-free water: to a final volume of 11 µL

    Step 1.3: Combine components for the DNA repair and end-prep reaction.

        Option 1.3.1: Prepare the reaction mix by combining the following components. Mix by pipetting and spin down.
            - DNA sample (from step 1.2): 11 µL
            - diluted DCS (from step 1.1): 1 µL
            - NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Buffer: 0.875 µL
            - Ultra II End-prep Reaction Buffer: 0.875 µL
            - Ultra II End-prep Enzyme Mix: 0.75 µL
            - NEBNext FFPE DNA Repair Mix: 0.5 µL

    Step 1.4: Incubate the DNA repair and end-prep reaction in a thermal cycler.

        Option 1.4.1: Incubate the reaction from step 1.3 at 20°C for 5 minutes, then at 65°C for 5 minutes.

    Step 1.5: Perform the first clean-up of the end-prepped DNA.

        Option 1.5.1: Add AMPure XP Beads to the reaction mix.
            - DNA repair and end-prep reaction (from step 1.4): 15 µL
            - AMPure XP Beads: 15 µL

    Step 1.6: Incubate the sample with beads.

        Option 1.6.1: Incubate the mixture from step 1.5 on a rotator mixer for 5 minutes at room temperature.

    Step 1.7: Wash the beads to remove contaminants.

        Option 1.7.1: Place the tube on a magnetic rack, remove the supernatant, and wash the bead pellet twice.
            - 80% ethanol in nuclease-free water: 200 µL

    Step 1.8: Elute the end-prepped DNA from the beads.

        Option 1.8.1: Resuspend the bead pellet in nuclease-free water.
            - nuclease-free water: 10 µL

    Step 1.9: Incubate to facilitate elution.

        Option 1.9.1: Incubate the suspension from step 1.8 for 2 minutes at room temperature.

    Step 1.10: Collect the eluted, end-prepped DNA.

        Option 1.10.1: Place the tube on a magnetic rack and transfer the supernatant containing the end-prepped DNA to a new tube.

Part 2: Native Barcode Ligation

    Step 2.1: Set up the native barcode ligation reaction.

        Option 2.1.1: Prepare the ligation reaction by combining the following components. Mix by pipetting and spin down.
            - end-prepped DNA (from step 1.10): 7.5 µL
            - Native Barcode: 2.5 µL
            - Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix: 10 µL

    Step 2.2: Incubate the barcode ligation reaction.

        Option 2.2.1: Incubate the reaction from step 2.1 for 20 minutes at room temperature.

    Step 2.3: Stop the ligation reaction.

        Option 2.3.1: Add EDTA to the reaction.
            - EDTA (blue cap): 4 µL

    Step 2.4: Pool all barcoded samples.

        Option 2.4.1: Combine all individual barcoded sample reactions (from step 2.3) into a single tube.

    Step 2.5: Perform a clean-up of the pooled barcoded library.

        Option 2.5.1: Add AMPure XP beads to the pooled sample.
            - Pooled barcoded library (from step 2.4): 1 volume
            - AMPure XP Beads: 0.4 volumes

    Step 2.6: Incubate the pooled library with beads.

        Option 2.6.1: Incubate the mixture from step 2.5 on a rotator mixer for 10 minutes at room temperature.

    Step 2.7: Wash the beads to remove contaminants from the pooled library.

        Option 2.7.1: Place the tube on a magnetic rack, remove the supernatant, and wash the bead pellet twice.
            - 80% ethanol in nuclease-free water: 700 µL

    Step 2.8: Elute the barcoded DNA library from the beads.

        Option 2.8.1: Resuspend the bead pellet in nuclease-free water.
            - nuclease-free water: 35 µL

    Step 2.9: Incubate to facilitate elution of the barcoded library.

        Option 2.9.1: Incubate the suspension from step 2.8 for 10 minutes at 37°C, flicking gently every 2 minutes.

    Step 2.10: Collect the eluted, barcoded DNA library.

        Option 2.10.1: Place the tube on a magnetic rack and transfer the supernatant containing the barcoded DNA library to a new tube.

Part 3: Adapter Ligation and Clean-up

    Step 3.1: Set up the adapter ligation reaction.

        Option 3.1.1: Prepare the reaction mix by combining the following components in order. Mix by pipetting and spin down.
            - barcoded DNA library (from step 2.10): 30 µL
            - Native Adapter: 5 µL
            - NEBNext Quick Ligation Reaction Buffer: 10 µL
            - Quick T4 DNA Ligase: 5 µL

    Step 3.2: Incubate the adapter ligation reaction.

        Option 3.2.1: Incubate the reaction from step 3.1 for 20 minutes at room temperature.

    Step 3.3: Perform a clean-up of the adapter-ligated library.

        Option 3.3.1: Add AMPure XP beads to the reaction.
            - Adapter ligation reaction (from step 3.2): 50 µL
            - AMPure XP Beads: 20 µL

    Step 3.4: Incubate the library with beads.

        Option 3.4.1: Incubate the mixture from step 3.3 on a rotator mixer for 10 minutes at room temperature.

    Step 3.5: Wash the beads with buffer to select for fragment size.

        Option 3.5.1: Wash the beads twice to retain DNA fragments of all sizes.
            - Short Fragment Buffer: 125 µL

    Step 3.6: Elute the final DNA library from the beads.

        Option 3.6.1: Resuspend the bead pellet in Elution Buffer.
            - Elution Buffer: 15 µL

    Step 3.7: Incubate to facilitate final library elution.

        Option 3.7.1: Incubate the suspension from step 3.6 for 10 minutes at 37°C, flicking gently every 2 minutes.

    Step 3.8: Collect the final prepared DNA library.

        Option 3.8.1: Place the tube on a magnetic rack and transfer the supernatant containing the prepared DNA library to a new tube.

    Step 3.9: Adjust the final library concentration for loading.

        Option 3.9.1: Dilute the prepared library to the final loading volume.
            - prepared DNA library (from step 3.8): 1 volume
            - Elution Buffer: to a final volume of 12 µL

Part 4: Priming and Loading the SpotON Flow Cell

    Step 4.1: Prepare the flow cell priming mix.

        Option 4.1.1: Combine the following reagents to create the priming mix.
            - Flow Cell Flush: 1170 µL
            - Bovine Serum Albumin: 5 µL
            - Flow Cell Tether: 30 µL

    Step 4.2: Insert the MinION and GridION Flow Cell into the sequencing device.

        Option 4.2.1: Insert the flow cell under the clip and press down firmly to ensure correct contact.

    Step 4.3: Remove any air bubbles from the priming port.

        Option 4.3.1: Set a P1000 pipette to 200 µL, insert the tip into the priming port, and turn the wheel to draw back 20-30 µL of buffer to remove any visible air bubbles.

    Step 4.4: Perform the first prime of the flow cell.

        Option 4.4.1: Add priming mix to the flow cell.
            - flow cell priming mix (from step 4.1): 800 µL

    Step 4.5: Prepare the final DNA library for loading.

        Option 4.5.1: Combine the following components in a new tube to create the library loading mix.
            - Sequencing Buffer: 37.5 µL
            - Library Solution: 25.5 µL
            - Final prepared library (from step 3.9): 12 µL

    Step 4.6: Complete the flow cell priming.

        Option 4.6.1: Add the remaining priming mix to the flow cell priming port.
            - flow cell priming mix (from step 4.1): 200 µL

    Step 4.7: Load the prepared library onto the flow cell.

        Option 4.7.1: Add the library loading mix dropwise into the SpotON sample port.
            - library loading mix (from step 4.5): 75 µL

    Step 4.8: Close the flow cell ports and start the sequencing run.

        Option 4.8.1: Replace the SpotON sample port cover, close the priming port, place the light shield on the flow cell, close the device lid, and start the run in the MinKNOW software.
